headings.usage: H1-H4, stats numbers, labels, terminal output, navigation

visual_enhancers.surfaces: Retro-Futurism / Terminal Look. Solid dark backgrounds with crisp 1px borders. No soft shadows. Use subtle glowing green text-shadows or box-shadows on active states.
visual_enhancers.effects: Terminal logs should have a black background with green text. Use a subtle repeating linear gradient (scanlines) if possible.

grids_layouts.bento_grid: For stats cards: col-span-1. For Job History/Terminal: col-span-3 or col-span-4.
grids_layouts.spacing_philosophy: Compact in dashboard data views (gap-4, p-4), highly generous in landing/educational areas (py-24, gap-12).

components.buttons: Sharp corners (rounded-none or rounded-sm). Primary button uses #22C55E background with black text. Hover state brightens.
components.inputs: Dark background (#000000), 1px zinc border, focus green ring. Use Shadcn components but strip soft rounding.
components.cards: border border-zinc-800 bg-[#0A0A0A] p-6. No drop shadow, completely flat.
components.terminal_log: Black box, JetBrains Mono green text, overflow-y-auto, glowing borders.

motion.hover: Instant color changes or rapid transitions. Avoid slow/soft transitions for the tech vibe.
motion.entrance: Staggered fade in for dashboard widgets (framer-motion).
motion.terminal: Simulate typing or instant appending for the real-time logs.

media.icons: lucide-react (Technical icons like Terminal, Activity, Globe, Shield, Cpu)

accessibility.contrast: Ensure green on black passes APCA/WCAG. Avoid pure white text on pure black to reduce eye strain; use #F4F4F5 instead.
accessibility.data_testid: Add data-testid attributes to all interactive elements.

instructions_to_main_agent: CRITICAL: You are working with .js files, NOT .tsx files. Write all React code as JSX (.js or .jsx extension).
Build a hybrid app: Landing area at the top with an Educational Disclaimer, followed by the main YouTube Booster dashboard tool, and educational sections at the bottom.
Use Shadcn UI components extensively for complex forms (duration inputs, location selectors), but adapt them to .js and strip out Vercel-like rounded borders to match the Terminal vibe.
Location Selector must allow: 'Random Worldwide', 'Auto-match audience', or 'Specific list' via Select/Dropdown.
Dashboard must include a 'Live Job Status' widget showing current IP address, Tor node status (country flag), and video progress (rotates every 3 videos).
Log stream must visually mimic a terminal: monospace green text on black bg, auto-scrolling.
Do not use generic gray borders everywhere. Use #27272A and ensure high contrast.
Include data-testid on every button, input, and interactive UI piece.
Use JetBrains Mono for headings and numeric stats, IBM Plex Sans for body text.
Ensure Tor rotation feature is clearly visualized in the UI (e.g. 'Next IP rotation in: X videos').
UNIVERSAL_GUIDELINES_FOR_MAIN_AGENT: Do not use completely transparent backgrounds over images; use solid dark overlays.
Avoid the generic 'Vercel look' (white/gray soft cards). Stick to the Terminal/Tech aesthetic.
No generic centered alignments for main dashboard content. Left-align data for readability.
Create depth through border colors and subtle text glows instead of box-shadows.
All interactive elements must have clear hover states.
For toasts, use Sonner if needed, styled dark to match.
Ensure all code generated is in JS/JSX, not TypeScript.
